text:
Maya Chen: Quick Q — embeddings endpoint contract for mixed inputs & truncation. I’m updating PR #482 and want to lock down behavior: do we accept non-string inputs (e.g., token arrays or bytes)? How exactly do we truncate (chars vs tokens, head vs tail) and what are the batch limits? Also want to confirm guaranteed output vector shape when inputs vary in length. cc @Jason Liu @Priya Rao

Jason Liu: For the public API today we only accept list of strings under `input`. We reject non-string types with 400. Tokenized ints / byte inputs are planned as a separate capability (not backwards-compatible) — we should expose that via a new param or endpoint in a future minor.

Truncation: server-side truncation is token-based (our SentencePiece tokenizer) and we truncate by keeping the head (first N tokens) to preserve prefix caching. Default per-item max_tokens is 8192 for the model family; if truncated we include per-item meta `truncated: true` and `truncation_mode: "head"`.

Jason Liu: Also: output vector dimension D is fixed per model (e.g., 768 for `embed-base-1`). Response shape is always `data` array of length == len(input), each element contains `embedding` (length D) and `meta` (object). Empty string => return a zero-vector (all 0s) and meta `empty: true` so clients can detect.

Maya Chen: Are we explicit about truncation suffix vs prefix in docs? Prefix truncation is important for our prefix cache.

Dylan Park: We truncate head (keep the first N tokens). Confirmed with perf runs. Example request/response I used in integration tests: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "input": ["<very long document...>", "short one"] }

Response:
{
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.001, -0.234, ..., 0.045], "meta": {"truncated": true, "truncation_mode": "head", "original_tokens": 12000}},
    {"embedding": [0.123, -0.111, ..., -0.002], "meta": {}}
  ]
}
```
Notes: embedding array length == model dim (constant). For empty string input we return `[0.0, 0.0, ...]` and `meta: {"empty": true}` so downstream code doesn't mistake it for a valid vector.

Priya Rao: Batch limits question — what's enforced server-side? Is it N items OR aggregated tokens? We need a clear contract so SDKs can auto-chunk. Also what error code when exceeded? 413? 429?

Jason Liu: Current soft limits: 512 items per request OR aggregated tokens <= 100,000 tokens. If either limit is exceeded we return 413 Payload Too Large with `error.reason = "batch_limit_exceeded"` and header `x-embed-limit-info: items=512,tokens=100000`. For Dedicated customers these are configurable via queue policies. We'll document both limits explicitly.

Priya Rao: Good — SDK plan: implement automatic chunking based on both metrics (items and token estimates). We should surface server header so SDKs can adapt. Also propose a helper to split long inputs along sentence boundaries before truncating to improve embedding quality.

Maya Chen: Backcompat: if we introduce `token_input` later, should we accept `input` as array-of-arrays (ints) in the same endpoint? Or create `/v1/embeddings/tokenized`?

Dylan Park: I vote for a new endpoint or explicit negotiation header `x-embed-format: string|tokens`. Mixing formats on the same `input` array would be messy and surprising. Keep `input: [string]` stable. New endpoint avoids ambiguity and makes validation simpler.

Jason Liu: Agreed. Plan: keep current `input: [string]` contract for this version. Add a feature RFC to introduce `POST /v1/embeddings/tokenized` and a negotiation header for clients that want advanced token inputs. Also add a migration note for SDKs.

Priya Rao: On output shape: confirm `data` array order must match input order (no internal reordering or sharding changes). And even in streaming/batched processing, we must return null or zero-vectors for inputs that failed rather than shifting positions. SDKs rely on index alignment.

Jason Liu: Yes — guarantee: index-aligned `data` output. For per-item failures (e.g., unsupported charset), we return `embedding: null` and `meta.error` set with details; overall request still 200 if at least one item succeeded, otherwise 4xx. We'll add that to the API doc section.

Dylan Park: Small but important: non-UTF8 bytes — server will respond 400 with `error.details = "invalid_encoding"`. We should add a test case for that. Also confirm we trim leading/trailing whitespace before tokenization.

Maya Chen: Action items? I can update PR #482 with the truncation/head behavior and meta fields.

Jason Liu: Action list: @Dylan — add unit/integration tests for head truncation, empty-string zero vector, non-utf8 rejection. @Priya — update py/js SDK chunker and add sentence-split helper; add docs for `x-embed-limit-info` header. @Maya — update PR description and include example responses. I'll file a small RFC about tokenized endpoint.

deploy-bot: CI: 12 tests passed on branch embed-truncation; deployed test build to staging (staging.eng-ml.redwood.internal). :white_check_mark:

Maya Chen: Thanks all — updating branch now. Marking as async, ping if any blockers.
